revisions.from: Eight Felda deals were audited in 2019. MACC opened papers on seven of them in 2026. / ...opened investigation papers on seven of the same deals / MACC's seven Felda files, announced on 2 September 2026, cover seven of the eight deals... / Seven of the eight deals were audited in 2019 and investigated in 2026...
revisions.to: Headline: 'Eight Felda deals were audited in 2019. In 2026 MACC has files open on seven of them.' Context and fact card 3 now state the composition: six new files opened 2 September 2026 on information received 24 August, plus one file open since 2017; seven of the eight audited deals are under investigation.
revisions.why: External Stage 3 graded the headline and two cards INCORRECT: MACC opened SIX new papers in 2026 and is still working ONE older Park City Grand Plaza paper. 'Seven opened in 2026' was wrong. Source: BERNAMA 2 September 2026 [S32], corroborated by The Edge [S2]. This was the most consequential error in the draft and my in-session pass missed it because it accepted the six-plus-one reconciliation without noticing the cards still said seven were opened.

revisions.from: It covered eight Felda and FIC purchases and was annexed to the FELDA White Paper, Command Paper 6 of 2019. / ...Ernst & Young delivered one in 2019, and Parliament has had it since.
revisions.to: Its 26-page summary report on the eight deals was annexed to the FELDA White Paper, tabled on 10 April 2019. / ...Ernst & Young finished one in 2019. Parliament has had the summary since.
revisions.why: External Stage 3 graded 'annexed in full' an OVERCLAIM: Lampiran 1 identifies itself as 'Ringkasan Laporan Bertarikh 4 April 2019', a 26-page summary. Nothing establishes that the full report or working papers were tabled. 'Summary' is now stated in both hook fields. The tabling date 10 April 2019 is added because the Parliament order paper [S35] and the 2020 written reply [S34] both confirm it, closing brief contradiction C1.

revisions.from: Ernst & Young found RM4.38 billion committed across the eight deals. Roughly half of it, about RM2.2 billion, was already written off.
revisions.to: Ernst & Young put the original value of the deals it could quantify at RM4.4 billion, and loss and impairment at about RM2.2 billion.
revisions.why: External Stage 3 graded 'written off' INCORRECT and 'committed' MISLEADING. Paparan 1 labels the RM4,382m as original investment value across the seven quantified deals (KLVC carries no comparable amount), and the RM2,208m is RM2,116m recorded impairment plus RM92m identified for recognition. Impairment is not a completed write-off. The card now uses EY's own categories: 'original value', 'loss and impairment', and 'the deals it could quantify'.

revisions.from: Mohd Isa Abdul Samad's conviction became final on 26 June 2026, nearly nine years after MACC opened its first Felda hotel files in 2017. / Felda also sued 21 defendants for RM2 billion over the Jalan Semarak land in 2019. It was still in pretrial applications in 2025.
revisions.to: Mohd Isa Abdul Samad's conviction concerns a Kuching hotel purchase that is not one of the eight audited deals. / The Federal Court restored it on 10 February 2026 and refused a review on 26 June. Felda's RM2 billion Jalan Semarak suit, filed in 2019, had not reached trial by 2025.
revisions.why: Two flags. External Stage 2 and Stage 3 both graded the card MISLEADING FRAMING because it sat beside the eight-deal discussion without saying the conviction concerned a different hotel (Merdeka Palace Hotel & Suites, Kuching); the caveat is now the card's lead sentence. External Stage 3 also supplied the restoration date, 10 February 2026 (PP v Mohd Isa Abdul Samad [2026] 3 MLRA 274 [S33]), and corrected '26 June' from 'became final' to 'refused a review'. The 'nearly nine years' span and '21 defendants' are dropped for budget; the 2019 filing and 2025 status remain.

revisions.from: Seven of the eight deals were audited in 2019 and investigated in 2026. The seven years in between are the finding nobody commissioned.
revisions.to: After the audit the state funded Felda's recovery and sued over one of the eight deals. Criminal enforcement on the eight is still open seven years on.
revisions.why: External Stage 3 graded the original MISLEADING: it implied an action-free interval, but MACC investigated Kensington and Grand Borneo in 2017, one paper stayed open, Felda filed the KLVC suit in 2019, and a 7 December 2020 written reply [S34] documents a recovery plan, government financial support and a monitoring task force. The defensible thesis is delayed and incomplete criminal enforcement, not inaction. The rewrite states what did follow and names the part that did not close. This is a value restructuring (the state's response was financial, not prosecutorial), so it still functions as a reframe.

revisions.from: Malaysia audited Felda more closely than almost any agency it owns. Scrutiny was never what failed. Follow-through was. / While the deals were being written down, the White Paper recorded settlers waiting on delayed Sara Hidup and Pendahuluan Hasil payments.
revisions.to: Felda has had a forensic audit, a recovery plan and a civil suit. Scrutiny was never what failed. Follow-through was. / The White Paper tied Felda's cash crisis to delayed Sara Hidup and Pendahuluan Hasil payments to settlers.
revisions.why: The comparative absolute 'more closely than almost any agency it owns' was flagged by external Stage 2 (OVERCLAIM; Tabung Haji, 1MDB and MARA have had comparable scrutiny) and external Stage 3 (UNVERIFIED; no denominator). Replaced with three documented facts. The sub is rewritten so the causal link is the White Paper's own (Ringkasan Eksekutif p.1: payment delays 'disebabkan aliran tunai FELDA yang kritikal'), which answers external Stage 2's economic-framing flag by naming the mechanism, and respects external Stage 3's point that no source ties post-2019 enforcement delay to settler harm. 'Written down' is replaced because of the impairment correction above.

revisions.from: Only the Indonesian plantation stake is missing. MACC began probing the Kensington purchase in 2017 and says that file is still open.
revisions.to: Only the PT Eagle High Plantations stake is absent. MACC says the cases are at an early stage and no corruption value has been set.
revisions.why: External Stage 3 asked that the omitted deal be named rather than described, and listed as an omitted fact MACC's own statement that the six new cases are at an early stage with no corruption value determined. That due-process qualifier is now on the card. The Kensington-since-2017 point moved to the card's big field as 'one file open since 2017'.

ba and fc now carry the external scores (bias_score 35 inverted; factual_accuracy_score 61) as the pipeline requires. pa is lowered from 84 to 78 because the external reviews found a load-bearing counting error and two classification errors in Stage 1 that the in-session passes did not catch. sr is 82: every flag from both external reviews is actioned or explicitly declined below, and no card now carries a claim graded INCORRECT, MISLEADING or UNVERIFIED by either reviewer; it is not higher because the in-session round had already declared the piece clean once.
The corrected headline is slightly less stark than the erroneous one, so the gap between headline and full picture narrows a little.

not_actioned.why: Card now says 'had not reached trial by 2025', which is the plain-language equivalent of vacated trial dates pending an interlocutory application and avoids a term most readers would not parse. The precise term is in the brief.

not_actioned.flag: External Stage 3: name Merdeka Palace Hotel & Suites on the card.
not_actioned.why: Budget. 'A Kuching hotel purchase that is not one of the eight audited deals' carries the caveat that matters; the hotel's name is in the brief and both stage files.

sr_justification: Round 2 applied seven corrections traced to specific external flags, the most important being the six-plus-one composition of MACC's files, which had been wrong in the headline. Every remaining card claim is one both external reviewers either verified or did not contest, and the four items declined are recorded with reasons. The piece is now less categorical and more accurate: the thesis moved from 'nothing followed the audit' to 'what followed was financial rescue and one civil suit, while criminal enforcement on the eight stayed open', which the record supports and which both reviewers said was the defensible version.
